MemoryConfigs.Name: Charm Aura Zone Transition Fix - Hook
MemoryConfigs.Description: REVERTS the 2026-08-17 reorder experiment back to the long-shipped value: jmp to the gear-reapply prefix cave at 3630E0, which calls sub_1402D67E0 and then falls through into the charm cave at 149B2B1. The reorder (hook pointing straight at 149B2B1, charm cave's terminal jmp retargeted to a tail cave at 35F63C) was based on a wrong root cause and bought nothing, so it is undone rather than left in - it changed when gear auras re-arm for no benefit. Replaces E8 rel32 CALL with E9 rel32 JMP; the stolen call sub_1402EC080 is performed inside the charm cave.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Charm Aura Zone Transition Fix - Cave
MemoryConfigs.Description: ONE CHANGE from the long-shipped version: the 12 bytes at cave offset 190 (RVA 149B36F) - test rax,rax / je 149B37C / mov qword [rax],0 - are replaced with 12x 0x90. That mov was the 'NULL [pItem+0x88]+0 (pStatListEx->pUnit)' step. Nulling the owner forced sub_1401E5EA0 down its full re-attach branch, and sub_1401E4EA0 begins by calling sub_1401E4300 on the charm's statlist, which UNLINKS it from the player and propagates a NEGATIVE delta for every stat it carries (sub_1401E4120(parent, key, -value, ...) at 1E4503 and 1E453F). That drives the player's aggregate item_singleskill/item_nonclassskill for the charm's oskill to 0, which fires the statlist fcallback sub_1402D2B00 case 97/107 on its removal branch: LEFT slot re-pointed to Attack via sub_140219690 @2D327A, RIGHT slot via sub_14029A2A0(unit,0,0,-1) @2D3316. The stats are then re-added by the same call, so the skill node and its level come back - but nothing re-selects the mouse slot. That is the whole bug, and it is why reordering the two passes changed nothing: the blip happens inside the charm loop wherever it runs. With the null write gone, sub_1401E5EA0 sees owner == pUnit and takes its enable/disable toggle branch instead, which for an already-enabled charm is a complete no-op and for a disabled one only propagates POSITIVE deltas - no unmerge, no blip either way. The aura re-arm is unaffected because it does not depend on the re-merge: the per-charm call at cave offset 216 goes to Multi-Aura Reactivation cave A (35C3AC), whose cave B (387090) walks the charm's own statlist entries and calls sub_2999E0 directly for every item_aura (151) layer. Also removes a latent crash: the je at offset 193 targeted 149B37C, one byte PAST the end of the 7-byte mov, i.e. into the middle of the following instruction - it would have jumped off-boundary had a charm ever had a null statlist pointer. Verified: 253/253 bytes decode linearly, no internal branch now lands off an instruction boundary, terminal jmp still 2A0424 at offset 248.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Cube Transmute Crash Fix - Hook
MemoryConfigs.Description: Hooks sub_140BE94B0 (the client-side transmute packet builder). Redirects to cave at 149B3B0 which counts cube items via sub_140208330 inventory walk and aborts the transmute if count > 100. Prevents crash from 5*N+8 byte packet exceeding the 512-byte cap in sub_14010E710's dedup buffer (asserts and exits at >=512 bytes, which manifests as a deferred crash in NVIDIA NGX during process teardown). No legitimate recipe takes >100 inputs; this is purely a misclick guard for cubes used as bulk storage. Stolen byte: mov [rsp+8], rbx.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Cube Transmute Crash Fix - Cave
MemoryConfigs.Description: Cave at 149B3B0 (167 bytes). On entry to sub_140BE94B0: gets pPlayer via sub_14006B050(dword_141D442D8), gets pInventory via sub_140208330. Walks pInventory linked list (chain through pItemData+0xB0). For each item with unitType==4 and pItemData->pageByte==3 (cube page), increments counter. If count > 100, returns immediately (transmute aborted). Otherwise re-executes stolen byte (mov [rsp+8], rbx) and jumps back to BE94B5 to let original transmute proceed. Stack: sub rsp, 0x28 for shadow space + alignment around the two calls; restored before ret or jmp back.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Cube Throw Crash Fix - Hook
MemoryConfigs.Description: Hooks sub_14010E930 (cube-drop packet builder, packet ID 0x22). Only ever called from sub_1400D35B0's actual drop send-site, so does NOT fire on movement/polling paths. Redirects to cave at 149B444 which checks (r9-r8)/16 = item count and aborts the packet send if count > 70. Prevents crash from 7*N+17 byte packet exceeding the 512-byte cap in sub_14010E710's dedup buffer (asserts and exits at >=512 bytes). Stolen bytes (9): push rbx (with REX 40 prefix), sub rsp, 0x750. Replaces previous failed cube-throw guard at sub_1400D35B0 entry which incorrectly fired on every-frame polling calls.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Cube Throw Crash Fix - Cave
MemoryConfigs.Description: Cave at 149B444 (33 bytes). Computes item count from r9-r8 (param registers a4-a3, the array end and start pointers, each item is 16 bytes / __m128i). If count > 70, returns 0 immediately (sub_14010E930 returns int; 0 = no error from packet send wrapper's perspective). Otherwise re-executes stolen prolog (push rbx; sub rsp, 0x750) and jumps back to 10E939. Massively simpler than previous attempt because we hook at the packet-send level rather than the cube-throw handler entry, eliminating the every-frame polling problem entirely.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Charm Dedup Group by item CODE {c11,c12} - Cave
MemoryConfigs.Description: Replaces the old 'Charm Dedup Group {2235,2236}' cave at 35C1E0, which matched on ITEM CLASS IDS and silently broke when new items shifted them: c11 is now classId 2236 and c12 is 2237, so the hardcoded pair was grouping c11 with whatever item landed on 2237's old slot and missing c12 entirely. This version matches on the items.txt CODE column, which is unique across all items and can never shift. Lives in the freed cltdofunc=83 body sub_14019D710 (ApplyRoyalStrikeLvl2, usable 19D710..19D98B = 636 bytes; body ends with CC padding 19D98C..19D98F and the next function starts at 19D990). Structure is otherwise identical to the old cave: rbx=pItem, rdi=pUnit on entry; on a non-group item it falls through to the original unique-row cave via jmp 149B467 (unchanged behaviour, including non-unique -> usable); on a group item it pushes r12/r14/r15, subs 0x28, gets the inventory via sub_140208330(pUnit), and walks the [pItemData+0xB0] chain requiring each candidate to be UNIT_ITEM ([r12]==4), have valid pItemData, nInvPage ([+0x55])==0 and no BROKEN/NOEQUIP ([+0x18]&0x4100). Tie-break is unchanged (cmp r12,rbx / jb fail - lowest pItem address wins), as is the WIN path (clear bit 0x80000000 in [pItemData+0x18], return 1) and the FAIL path (set that loser bit for the renderer cave at 149B55B, then unmerge the charm's stats via sub_1401E4300 on [pItem+0x88], return 0). The only change is the group test, which is now a shared subroutine at 19D7DC: given a classId in ecx it bounds-checks against the item count, computes record = itemsTable + 436*classId, reads the code dword at record+0x80, and returns 1 for 'c11 ' (0x20313163) or 'c12 ' (0x20323163). Both the entry test and the per-candidate test call it, so the two charms form one exclusive set - one active total regardless of how many of each are carried. Item table base and count are read RIP-relative from 141CA0390 / 141CA0398 so the patch is ASLR-safe. Code offset 0x80 was confirmed live: 0x80/0x84/0x88/0x8C are code/normcode/ubercode/ultracode and read identically on these charms, 3-char codes are space-padded (0x20). cm8/cm9 were deliberately EXCLUDED - those charms are no longer obtainable.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Charm Dedup - Cave (IsCharmUsable)
MemoryConfigs.Description: Cave at 0x149B467 (244 bytes). Saves r12/r14/r15. Returns 1 if pItem->pItemData->dwQuality (+0x00) != 7 (UNIQUE). Else reads my unique row from pItemData+0x34 into r14d, gets pInventory via sub_208330, walks linked list via [pItemData+0xB0]. For each other item: must be UNIT_ITEM, valid pItemData, dwQuality==7, nInvPage(+0x55)==0, no IFLAG_BROKEN(0x100)/IFLAG_NOEQUIP(0x4000), same dwUniqueRow. Tie-break: cmp r12,rbx; jb .fail (lower pItem address loses). On .ok (winner): clears bit 0x80000000 in [pItemData+0x18] and returns 1. On .fail (loser): sets bit 0x80000000 in [pItemData+0x18] (loser marker, read by sub_9FFF0 cave for red render), then loads pStatListEx from [pItem+0x88] and calls sub_1E4300 to expire/unmerge stats from owner before returning 0. Returns to 0x2005C7.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Bow/missile damage 32-bit imul overflow fix - hook
MemoryConfigs.Description: Hook at RVA 3C65B6. Original 19 bytes are: imul ecx,[r14]; imul ecx (with 0x51EB851F); sar edx,5; mov eax,edx; shr eax,1Fh; add edx,eax; add [r14],edx. This computes ecx*(*r14)/100 with rounding then adds to *r14. r14 = damage_struct + 0x1C (physical damage component). ecx = damage bonus percent. The 32-bit imul ecx,[r14] overflows int32 for high damage values (e.g. 50M raw * 100 = 5B exceeds INT32_MAX), wrapping to negative which then gets divided and added, producing negative or wrong damage components. Replaces with JMP to cave at RVA 149BD96 which performs equivalent math in 64-bit with INT32 saturation. Returns to RVA 3C65C9.

MemoryConfigs.Name: Bow/missile damage 32-bit imul overflow fix - cave

MemoryConfigs.Name: Faster cast rate ceiling raised to 500 FCR
MemoryConfigs.Description: Vanilla clamps the cast animation rate at 175 percent, which the diminishing-return curve reaches at exactly 200 faster cast rate - every point past 200 is dead. The clamp lives in sub_14020A760, the merged animation-rate updater, at RVA 20A82A: 'mov eax, 0AFh' (175) feeding 'cmp ecx,eax / cmovg ecx,eax' at 20A82F/20A831. Raising the immediate to 0C4h (196) moves the ceiling to the value the curve reaches at 500 FCR, so faster cast rate keeps paying all the way to 500 instead of stopping at 200.
